Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this. We're preparing to onboard our inference workload to a private VPC (on-prem region) and need Redwood to validate the control-plane/data-plane demarcation and egress proofing for compliance. Attached is a rough network sketch and a short note on data residency requirements. High level asks:

- Confirm that the control plane endpoints can be placed in our management segment (no direct internet egress from runtime nodes)
- Validate acceptable egress proxies and TLS terminations for auditability
- Acceptance criteria we can show to our compliance team for staging->prod cutover

Can we book ~45m next week for a brief walk-through?

Subject: Re: Private VPC review request — initial diagrams attached

Hi Sophie — thanks for the sketch, it's helpful. Quick answers up front and a couple scheduling options below.

Short answers:
- Yes, you can keep runtime (inference) nodes entirely within your private subnet with no internet egress; control plane traffic can be routed over a management VPN to the Redwood control endpoints we host in your VPC region.
- For auditability we recommend sidecar TLS passthrough to an egress proxy (mTLS to your proxy, logging at the proxy) plus prefix/KV caching disabled for regulated tokens.
- We'll produce a short acceptance checklist you can present to compliance (staging can be gated on selective canary traffic and telemetry verification).

I attached our reference doc that outlines recommended topology variants and required firewall rules. Can you confirm the following before the call?
1) Which CIDR(s) will the runtime hosts use?
2) Do you have an existing egress proxy that supports request-level logging and TLS termination?
3) Any explicit deny-lists or approved external endpoints we must permit?

Scheduling: I'm free Monday 11/24 10–11 PT or Tuesday 11/25 14–15 PT. I'll set up a calendar invite once you confirm.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-reference-v0.9.pdf

—
Naomi Feldman
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 Nov 2025 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Private VPC review request — internal prep notes

Internal — prep notes for call with Acme Health. Copying into the thread before I hit the meeting. Key items to verify and bring to the customer:

1) Control-plane endpoints and auth
- Control plane must be reachable from the management segment via outbound TLS. If they insist on private-only control plane, we can package a control-plane appliance (appliance image) but that requires additional license and 2x HA.

2) Data-plane (runtime) topology
- Runtime nodes isolated in customer tenant VLAN, no NAT to internet. All outbound allowed only to approved egress proxies.
- We'll recommend a network policy that restricts egress to the Redwood kernel update feed and your telemetry collector (list them explicitly).

3) Egress proofing & telemetry
- Egress proxy must emit per-request logs (time, source IP, target FQDN, TLS SNI) and forward to your SIEM.
- Recommend sidecar TLS passthrough or mTLS to the proxy; do not terminate in the runtime unless the customer has a certified HSM-backed KMS policy.

4) Canary & acceptance
- Canary plan: route 1% of production traffic through the new VPC deployment with token-level tracing enabled for 72 hours. Verify latency and quality regression thresholds.
- Acceptance checklist: health probes, KV cache disabled for regulated requests, audit logs for every control-plane action.

5) Operational handoff docs to provide: runbook for key rotation, KMS integration notes, rollback plan.

Attachments I'm drafting: egress-proofing-checklist.md, canary-rollout-plan.xlsx

On the call we should: confirm CIDR, confirm proxy capabilities, confirm compliance evidence format (csv logs vs syslog).

—Kimberly
Staff Infra Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Chan <sophie.chan@acme-health.com>, Lester O'Neil <lester@acme-health.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Nov 2025 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private VPC boundary-fit & topology acceptance review — proposed acceptance checklist and next steps

Hi Sophie / Lester — thanks for confirming a slot. Following our internal review (notes below) we've put together a concise acceptance checklist and next steps to make the staging->prod handoff auditable for your compliance team. I've attached the checklist PDF and included the key items inline.

Inline acceptance highlights (summary):
- Network: runtime nodes in private tenant VLAN, default-deny egress except to: your egress proxy, Redwood control endpoints (management VPN), and approved telemetry collectors. Provide exact CIDRs for each.
- Control plane: management VPN outbound from your management segment to Redwood control endpoints; mutual TLS with client certs issued by your PKI. If private-only control plane required, we will supply a control-plane appliance (additional procurement).
- Egress proofing: egress proxy must log per-request fields (timestamp, source IP, source port, destination FQDN, SNI, response code) and forward to your SIEM; logs retained for minimum 90 days (per your note).
- Cryptography: KMS-backed key storage for tenant secrets; we recommend HSM integrator for keys used in regulated workflows.
- Canary: 1% traffic for 72 hours with token-level traces retained; automated rollback if latency or quality regressions cross threshold.
- Observability: route-level traces, token-level cost/latency breakdowns, and model-version pinning for regression control.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-acceptance-checklist.pdf (short PDF version we think is compliance-friendly)

Next steps:
1) Sophie: confirm runtime CIDRs and whether your egress proxy supports the per-request fields above.
2) Lester: confirm retention window for egress logs and SIEM integration details.
3) Naomi / Kimberly: we'll produce a 2-page control-plane appliance spec if you prefer private-only control plane.
4) We'll hold the call Monday 11/24 10–10:45 PT (Calendly link) — invite sent.

Let us know if you'd like the checklist converted into a formal change control package.

Best,
Naomi
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
